purpose: Test whether a separately pre-registered term-level ranking method can reproduce source-labelled LION cases while separating metric-blind structural controls inside the measured BioASQ 2013 secondary snapshot.

not_a_claim_of: validity outside the biomedical academic literature represented by BioASQ

freeze_timing.disclosure: The source, case identities, mappings, and prior failed OpenAlex metrics were known before freeze. No support count, BioASQ pilot formula, score, rank, or held-out result was inspected.

case_population.heldout_disclosure: Held-out identities are public and known to the author. Held-out means score-unseen and excluded from formula choice or revision, not identity-blinded.

positives.population_definition: All five Cancer Discovery cases used in the LION evaluation and present in the pinned candidate ledger; no case was selected by a lacuna metric result.

controls.population_definition: Every entry in the pinned 16-item metric-blind negative review queue, preserving its proposed kind, cutoff, and split.

source_transform.direct_endpoint_cooccurrences: retain_and_report_exactly; never delete A-C articles for a named case
excluded_from_candidate_universe: descriptors absent from the cutoff slice
descriptors below the active minimum-support threshold
source_transform.ontology_relatives_policy: Do not remove parent, child, or sibling descriptors before ranking; the hard controls exist to measure that confounder.
source_transform.bridge_policy: The named B is a traceability diagnostic, not a supervised feature or label. Candidate methods must expose corpus-derived bridge terms for every evaluated target.

requirements: Every endpoint and named positive bridge resolves to exactly one pinned MeSH 2013 descriptor UI.
Every seed A and target C has at least 10 source articles at its primary cutoff.
Every target C belongs to the primary candidate universe for its seed and cutoff.
Every case records exact endpoint marginals, A-C cooccurrence, and named-positive bridge marginals without a ranking score.
source_compatibility_gate.replacement_policy: Do not replace, drop, or relabel an incompatible case after seeing support. Freeze a separately named successor protocol before any metric output if this source population is inadequate.

metric_inputs_may_not_include: named target identity as a feature
named positive bridge identity as a feature
metric_isolation.development_policy: Development cases may be inspected only after the initial formula contract is frozen. At most one documented formula revision is allowed.
metric_isolation.heldout_policy: Do not compute, cache, log, or persist held-out scores until the final post-development formula contract is frozen.

ranking_contract.primary_orientation: rank target C conditioned on seed A

heldout_decision_rule.evaluability_requirement: All 10 held-out cases pass the primary source-compatibility gate; otherwise the outcome is pilot_inconclusive_source_coverage.
heldout_decision_rule.positive_requirement: At least 1 of 2 held-out source-labelled LION targets ranks in the top 5 percent.
heldout_decision_rule.hard_control_requirement: Zero of 4 held-out ontology-sibling hard controls ranks in the top 5 percent.
heldout_decision_rule.distant_control_requirement: All 4 held-out cross-branch distant controls rank below the median, meaning rank_fraction > 0.5.
heldout_decision_rule.sensitivity_requirement: The three held-out requirements must also hold at minimum-support settings 5 and 20; an unevaluable sensitivity setting is not a pass.

reporting_requirements: Publish all development and held-out case ranks, eligible-universe sizes, rank fractions, endpoint marginals, exact A-C cooccurrence counts, and surfaced bridge terms.
Keep source-labelled positives, ontology-generated controls, and measured metric outputs structurally distinct.
Report every non-evaluable case without denominator shrinkage or post-result replacement.
Report primary and sensitivity outcomes even when they disagree.
A passing label supports only this BioASQ secondary-snapshot pilot signal and cannot be called metric-v3 validation or gap discovery.
limitations: BioASQ supplies a single 2013 secondary snapshot, not the missing 2007, 2011, 2012, and 2013 NLM baseline releases.
Filtering article publication year does not reconstruct the MeSH assignments visible at each historical cutoff; all descriptor identities are resolved through MeSH 2013.
The five positive cases are source-labelled LION reproduction cases and have not all passed independent discovery-truth adjudication.
The sixteen controls are metric-blind ontology proposals, not proof that a relation is absent in academic or non-academic knowledge.
Held-out identities are public, so a passing result is weaker than identity-blinded external validation.
BioASQ and MeSH omit or thinly represent craft, practitioner, indigenous, humanities, historical, and other non-academic knowledge.
No outcome from this protocol contributes metric-v3 readiness or authorizes an LLM interpretation layer.
